tools.name: hermes_retrieve_monitored_data
tools.description: TOOL: Retrieve monitored data for a specific API configuration. PURPOSE: Fetch the latest monitored data for a given configuration ID. This is STEP 3 of the monitoring setup process. PREREQUISITE: Must call validate_api_configuration() first and obtain a config_id from successful validation, then activate_monitoring() to start monitoring. This function can be called at any time after monitoring activation to retrieve the latest data collected by the monitoring system. ARGUMENTS: - config_id: The ID of the API configuration to retrieve data for (required) - mcp_api_key: User's MCP API key for verification (must match validation step). - mode: Data return mode - "summary" (LLM-optimized), "details" (full responses, minimal metadata), "full" (everything) Input Examples: 1. Retrieve data for stock monitoring: config_id: 123456789 mcp_api_key: "your_mcp_key_here" 2. Retrieve data for weather alerts: config_id: 987654321 mcp_api_key: "your_mcp_key_here". Returns: Dictionary with monitoring status in one of three formats based on mode parameter, , {, True,, "Weather Alert Monitor",, {, "active",  // "active", "inactive", "good",    // "good", "degraded", "no_data", 15,, 93.3,, "2025-06-05T15:20:00",, "2025-06-05T15:20:00", },, [, {, "2025-06-05T15:20:00",, true,, null,, "{'alerts': [{'type': 'tornado'}]}..."  // truncated to 150 characters, }, // ... up to 5 most recent calls, ],, 15,, {, 20,, false, }, }, , {, True,, "Weather Alert Monitor",, "active",, 15,, 93.3,, [, {, "2025-06-05T15:20:00",, true,, {...},  // full response data, null, }, // ... up to 10 most recent calls with full responses, ], }, , {, True,, "Weather Alert Monitor",, "Monitor severe weather alerts",, True,, False,, {...},, {...},, [...]  // all historical data, }, , {, False,, "Invalid config_id or mcp_api_key", }, If config_id not found or invalid, returns success=False with error message

tools.name: Router_MCP_handle_keyword_mcp_search
tools.description: Handle keyword-based search for MCP servers across selected sources. If the client (such as Cursor or Claude) encounters a task it cannot handle, it can use MCP to search for other tools that can. Use this search when you know the specific name or keywords of the MCP Server you're looking for. Returns: A dictionary containing the search results with the following keys:, results: List of found MCP servers with their configurations. Each configuration can be added to the MCP Client's config file to register the server., total: Total number of results, search_type: Type of search performed ("keyword")
